extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academics invited to review manuscripts for npj Complexity (peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reviewing research manuscripts submitted to npj Complexity: assess technical soundness, strength of evidence, and importance to the journal's specific field, while following confidentiality, anonymity and competing-interest policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: The data are technically sound
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the general criteria for publication in npj Complexity. Reviewers should evaluate the technical correctness and reliability of the data and analyses presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: The paper provides strong evidence for its conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper provides strong evidence for its conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the results and analyses presented convincingly support the authors' claims; evaluate appropriateness of methods, robustness of results, and whether alternative explanations are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript importance to the specific field
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript is important to scientists in the specific field covered by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the novelty, significance, and likely interest of the work to researchers in the journal's scope when recommending whether it merits publication in npj Complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information and balanced arguments for editorial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask that reviewers provide us with the information on which a decision should be based. Setting out the arguments for and against publication is often as helpful as a direct recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than only giving an accept/reject recommendation, set out clear arguments, strengths and weaknesses, and evidence that editors can use to weigh the paper against others under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be willing to provide follow-up advice if requested
rubrics_metrics.description: We may go back to reviewers for further advice, particularly in cases where there are disagreements, or where the authors believe they have been misunderstood on points of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreeing to review implies willingness to answer editor queries or clarify points raised in your report; however, reviewers are not expected to engage in prolonged disputes—editors will keep follow-up to the minimum necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to review subsequent revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When you agree to review a paper, we consider this a commitment to review subsequent revisions as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will assess revised papers and may not send them for re-review if authors have not seriously attempted to address previous criticisms. Reviewers should be prepared to evaluate revised manuscripts when invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be timely, careful and critical but fair
rubrics_metrics.description: For instance, we seek reviewers who are timely, careful and critical but fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors select reviewers who will meet deadlines, scrutinize technical and conceptual aspects rigorously, and provide balanced, impartial assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain strict confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask reviewers to treat the review process as strictly confidential, and not to discuss the manuscript with anyone not directly involved in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to consult with laboratory colleagues, but you must identify them to the editors when you submit your review. Consulting outside experts may be acceptable only after checking with the editors to avoid involving excluded individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and optional signing of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not release reviewer identities to authors or to other reviewers, except when you intentionally sign your comments to authors. Signing of reviewer reports is entirely voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer comments (signed or anonymous) are shared with the other reviewers. For reviewers preferring anonymity, the journal will neither confirm nor deny speculation about identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports will not be suppressed; avoid offensive or confidential disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of policy, we do not suppress reviewer comments to the authors; any comments that were intended for the authors are transmitted, regardless of what we may think of the content. On rare occasions, we may edit a report to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for constructive criticism and avoid language that causes needless offence. Understand that robustly expressed criticisms are not necessarily unfair, but avoid revealing confidential information or personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and avoid competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: We avoid reviewers whom the authors have excluded, for whatever reason, within our guidelines. We also avoid reviewers who have had recent or ongoing collaborations with the authors, who have commented on drafts of the manuscript, who are in direct competition to publish the same finding, who we know to have a history of dispute with the authors or who have a financial interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should draw the editors' attention to anything that might affect their review, and should decline to review if they cannot be objective or could be perceived to be biased. The policy recognizes that competing interests are not always clear-cut; declare borderline cases for the editors to decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors treat technical concerns seriously and may seek additional advice
rubrics_metrics.description: We take reviewers' criticisms very seriously, and in particular, we are very reluctant to disregard technical concerns. We may go back to reviewers for further advice... We may also occasionally bring in additional reviewers to resolve disputes, but we prefer to avoid doing so unless there is a specific issue on which we absolutely must have further advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise any technical issues clearly and with evidence, since editors will weigh such concerns heavily and may request further clarification or additional reviews to resolve disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection and decision-making process
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted manuscripts are read in full by the editors... we send only those papers that seem most likely to meet our criteria for publication to formal review... Reviewed manuscripts are sent to at least two, and typically three, reviewers. The editors consider the reviewers' advice when making a decision on the paper... Editorial decisions are not a matter of counting votes or numerical rank assessments, and we do not always follow the majority recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware that editors screen submissions before external review, and that editorial decisions are based on the strength of arguments and fit within the journal's priorities rather than simple majority recommendations. Provide clear, evidence-based arguments to aid editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria (why editors choose you)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection is critical to the review process, and we base our choice on many factors, including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and our own previous experience of a reviewer's performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that editors expect reviewers to have relevant expertise and a track record of reliable, high-quality reviews; being timely and fair improves likelihood of future invitations.
